text:
anya: quick thought after the last postmortem

propose we standardize a tiny handoff card that travels with the ticket. keeps ownership explicit and reduces the "who owns this now" drama. want sign-off before i add to the incident template. :clipboard:

vik: yes please. make the card tiny though. ack in 24h, plan update 72h, full check 30d sounds good.

tori: add an explicit backup and a one-line success criteria. if owner goes dark ops-bot should ping backup at T+24.

anya: here's a one-line JSON-like snippet we can paste into issues: 
```
handoff_card:
  owner: @vik
  backup: @tori
  due: 2026-05-10 (T+72)
  done_criteria: errors < 1% for 7d or rollback applied
  pattern_tag: db-connection-throttling
```

lee: rotation thought: make IC rotation formal monthly and require a secondary IC on shift. secondary to handle followups and be responsible for the handoff card if IC is overloaded. eases burnout.

milan: agreed. also suggest we measure "followup coverage": percent of followup cards with owners assigned within 48h and percent closed by due date. small dashboards are motivating.

vik: can we add a "recurrence" flag set when the same pattern shows up 3x in 90 days? route those to a pattern-owner board.

tori: ops-bot can create the followup card automatically on incident close and tag recurrence candidates at T+72 if the pattern appears in recent incidents. i can wire the webhook.

ops-bot: action: create handoff card for INC-2026-0509 at 2026-05-09T18:00Z (T+0). reminder to owner @vik at T+24 and to backup @tori at T+24 if no acknowledgement.

anya: communications: add a small comms section to the template (external point, internal status owner, 3-line status blurb). prevents ad-hoc replies during followups.

lee: also add a quarterly "pattern triage" slot owned by platform where pattern-owners present recurring issues and grooming picks priority items.

milan: +1. can we pilot these on the next two incidents before rolling into the runbook? small experiment, low friction.

anya: perfect. i'll PR the template and a tiny tracker column called "followup coverage". tagging @vik @tori @lee for quick review. thanks all :sparkles:
